transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah… I came in because I’m having a really hard time keeping things organized. I’m trying to manage my schoolwork and also a small accessories shop, and it feels like everything just turns into piles—supplies, receipts, assignment notes, due dates. I don’t know what to do first, and it’s been really overwhelming.
Have you struggled with organizing tasks and staying focused like this since you were a kid, or is this something that's more new for you recently?

It’s been there since I was a kid. My mom still has notes from elementary school where teachers wrote that I was always getting out of my seat, talking before they called on me, and rushing through group activities even when I knew the material. So it doesn’t feel new, it’s just causing more problems now.
These days, do you still notice yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or blurting things out—or has that mostly settled down as you've gotten older?

Yeah, I still feel pretty restless. Even if I’m just sitting there and not actually going anywhere, it feels like my body is kind of buzzing, like I need to move. It’s worse when I’m supposed to sit still and just listen to someone.
Do these organization and restlessness problems also cause issues in other areas of your life, like at home or in your relationships, not just at school or work?

Yeah, it’s not just school. It’s affecting bigger things. I missed some required steps for my program, and now my financial aid might be at risk, which is really stressful. And with my shop projects, people have started relying on me less because I don’t always keep up with what I said I’d do.

Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days where you felt unusually elated, irritable, or full of energy, needed much less sleep than usual, and had racing thoughts—separate from how you feel most of the time?

I don’t think so. I mean, I have times where I’m more keyed up or irritable, but I can’t think of a stretch of several days where I felt unusually great or energized and barely needed sleep like that.
Do you also experience excessive, hard-to-control worry about multiple things—like your health, finances, or performance—that goes beyond just feeling restless or disorganized?

I’m not really sure. I do worry about stuff sometimes, like anyone would, but I don’t know that it’s this constant, hard-to-control worrying about lots of different things. It feels more like I get stressed when things pile up or I’m dealing with consequences.
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes, losing important items, or forgetting appointments and tasks in your daily life?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I probably do some of that sometimes, but I haven’t really been keeping track of it or noticed a clear pattern.
Can you give me a specific recent example—like a time you lost something important (keys, phone, paperwork) or missed an appointment or deadline you didn't intend to miss?

Yeah, recently it’s been more like I can’t keep track of everything than one single thing. I’m trying to handle schoolwork and my little accessories shop, and my supplies, due dates, receipts, and assignment notes all just end up in piles. Then I’ll look at it and not know what I’m supposed to do first, so things get missed or left until the last minute.
Do you often find your mind wandering or have trouble staying focused during tasks, conversations, or lectures, even when you're trying to pay attention?

Yes, that happens a lot. Like in class, or if I’m watching a video for my business assignments, I’ll start out trying to listen, but after a few minutes my mind drifts to charm designs or order ideas. Then I realize I missed half of what was said.

Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you recall specific examples of these attention or hyperactivity problems—like the seat issues or blurting out you mentioned—actually happening at that age?

Yeah. My mom actually still has some notes from when I was in elementary school. They say I was always getting out of my seat, talking before I was called on, and rushing through group activities even when I knew how to do the work. So it was definitely happening back then too.
